src/screens/admin/AdminDashboardScreen.t.whatsWrong: `${order.total.toFixed(2)}` dereferences order.total with no guard. total is mapped from `order.totalUSD` (line 213) which maps from the nullable Postgres column `total_usd`. src/screens/admin/AdminDashboardScreen.t.rootCause: Mapping at line 213 (`total: order.totalUSD`) copies a nullable value into a field typed `number`, and the render assumes it is always numeric.
src/screens/admin/AdminDashboardScreen.t.failureScenario: Server returns a recent order with total_usd = null (walk-in order created but not yet totalled). Dashboard loads, renderOrderItem runs order.total.toFixed(2) -> TypeError -> screen crashes for the admin.
src/screens/admin/AdminDashboardScreen.t.fix: Guard at render: `${(order.total ?? 0).toFixed(2)}` and/or coalesce in the mapping: `total: order.totalUSD ?? 0`.

src/screens/admin/AdminDashboardScreen.t.whatsWrong: `order.status.toLowerCase()` inside the t() key has no guard. status is mapped from `order.status` (line 216) straight from the DB `status` column with no coalescing. A null/absent status crashes render with 'Cannot read property toLowerCase of null'. Note getStatusColor(order.status) on lines 302/304/332 survives (object lookup tolerates null), which masks the real crash site here.
src/screens/admin/AdminDashboardScreen.t.rootCause: This screen re-implements order mapping (211-218) and omits the `String(o.status||'pending')` guard that adminService.getRecentOrders (adminService.ts:498) uses for exactly this reason.
src/screens/admin/AdminDashboardScreen.t.failureScenario: Server returns an order row where status is null (bad import / migration gap). getStatusColor returns '#999' fine, but line 337 calls null.toLowerCase() -> TypeError -> dashboard crashes.
src/screens/admin/AdminDashboardScreen.t.fix: Coalesce in mapping: `status: order.status || 'pending'`, or at the call site: `` t(`admin.orders.status.${(order.status || '').toLowerCase()}`, { defaultValue: order.status || '' }) ``.

src/screens/admin/AdminDashboardScreen.t.whatsWrong: loadData captures tenantId in a closure but calls setStats/setRecentOrders/setStoreProfile unconditionally when it resolves, with no check that tenantId is still current. On a multi-tenant admin, switching tenant A->B while A's fetch is in flight (slow network) lets the late A response overwrite B's state, flashing tenant A's revenue and orders under tenant B — directly violating the app's tenant-isolation rule.
src/screens/admin/AdminDashboardScreen.t.rootCause: No request-generation/abort guard; results are applied regardless of whether the tenant that requested them is still selected.
src/screens/admin/AdminDashboardScreen.t.failureScenario: Admin who manages two businesses opens the dashboard for tenant A on a slow connection, then switches to tenant B before A's Promise.all resolves. A's stats/orders arrive last and setStats(A) renders A's money under B's header.
src/screens/admin/AdminDashboardScreen.t.fix: Capture the tenant per call and bail before writing: keep a `const activeTenantRef = useRef(tenantId)` updated in the tenant-change effect, snapshot `const reqTenant = tenantId` at the top of loadData, and wrap every setState with `if (reqTenant !== activeTenantRef.current) return;` (or use an incrementing requestId).

src/screens/admin/AdminEditDiscountScree.whatsWrong: The product-search filter calls p.partNumber.toLowerCase() unguarded. parts.part_number is TEXT (nullable) in schema.sql:35 and mapProduct (productService.ts:22) does `partNumber: data.part_number` with NO default, so partNumber can be null. Admin opens the discount editor, scrolls to Select Products, and types one character in the search field. For any product whose name does not match (short-circuit passes to partNumber), null.toLowerCase() throws -> red screen / app crash. (p.name is safe because parts.name is NOT NULL, schema.sql:32.)

.filter(p =>

  (p.name || '').toLowerCase().includes(productSearchQuery.toLowerCase()) ||

Also guard the display at line 614: `${product.partNumber || '—'} • $${product.priceUSD ?? 0}` so a null partNumber/price does not render the literal 'null'.

src/screens/admin/AdminEditDiscountScree.whatsWrong: The load effect depends only on [discountId]. Both loaders early-return when tenantId is falsy WITHOUT clearing loading state: loadProducts (line 82) leaves productsLoading=true (initialized true, line 72), and loadDiscount (line 96) leaves loading=true (initialized to isEditing, line 47). tenantId starts null in TenantContext (line 69) and resolves asynchronously, but the effect never re-runs when it resolves because tenantId is not a dependency.

A moment later tenantId resolves and re-renders, but deps [discountId] are unchanged so neither loader re-runs. Edit mode: the full-screen ActivityIndicator (lines 243-249) spins forever. src/screens/admin/AdminOperatingHoursScr.whatsWrong: getOperatingHours() returns `data.data as OperatingHours` — a raw JSONB column cast with no runtime validation. If the stored blob is missing a day key (older schema, partial save, hand-edited row), line 74 sets a schedule without e.g. `sunday`. src/screens/admin/AdminOperatingHoursScr.rootCause: `as OperatingHours` cast hides that server JSON may be partial/garbage; no per-day normalization before setState.
src/screens/admin/AdminOperatingHoursScr.failureScenario: DB global_settings.data = {"monday":{...},"tuesday":{...}} (5 days missing). Admin opens Operating Hours → immediate crash, screen unusable.
src/screens/admin/AdminOperatingHoursScr.fix: Normalize on load instead of trusting the cast. In fetchOperatingHours: `if (data) { setSchedule(prev => ({ ...prev, ...Object.fromEntries(DAYS.map(d => [d, { ...defaultSchedule, ...(data as any)[d] }])) })); }` and defensively in renderDayRow: `const daySchedule = schedule[day] ?? defaultSchedule;`

src/screens/admin/AdminOperatingHoursScr.whatsWrong: openTimePicker reads `schedule[day].openTime`/`closeTime` then `currentWaitTime.split(':').map(Number)`. If that time is undefined/null or a non-string (server garbage), `.split` throws. If it is a malformed string like '9am' or '9', split yields NaN for hours/minutes → `date.setHours(NaN)` makes an Invalid Date, which is then passed as `value` to Android DateTimePicker (line 237) and throws/misbehaves.
src/screens/admin/AdminOperatingHoursScr.rootCause: Time strings assumed to always be well-formed 'HH:mm'; no guard on missing/malformed values before split and Date construction.
src/screens/admin/AdminOperatingHoursScr.failureScenario: Row stored with openTime:null (or '9am'). Admin taps the open-time button → crash on split, or picker opens on Invalid Date.
src/screens/admin/AdminOperatingHoursScr.fix: `const raw = (mode === 'open' ? schedule[day]?.openTime : schedule[day]?.closeTime) || '09:00'; const [h, m] = String(raw).split(':').map(Number); const date = new Date(); date.setHours(Number.isFinite(h) ? h : 9, Number.isFinite(m) ? m : 0, 0, 0);`

src/screens/admin/AdminOperatingHoursScr.whatsWrong: handleTimeChange only sets `setShowPicker(false)` inside the `Platform.OS === 'android'` branch. src/screens/admin/AdminOperatingHoursScr.rootCause: iOS inline spinner needs an explicit confirm/cancel affordance; component provides none and never clears showPicker on iOS.
src/screens/admin/AdminOperatingHoursScr.failureScenario: iOS admin taps a time button → spinner appears at the bottom and cannot be closed; tapping other rows just leaves it open.
src/screens/admin/AdminOperatingHoursScr.fix: Wrap the iOS picker in a Modal with a 'Done' button that calls setShowPicker(false), or add an inline Done button. e.g. on iOS render the DateTimePicker plus a TouchableOpacity 'Done' that setShowPicker(false); keep the android auto-dismiss branch as-is.

src/screens/admin/AdminStoreLocationsScr.whatsWrong: `item.type.toUpperCase()` assumes `type` is always a non-null string. `mapDbToLocation` (locationService.ts:155) sets `type: data.type` with no validation/default, so a null or missing `type` column on a store_locations row throws `TypeError: Cannot read property 'toUpperCase' of null`, which crashes the entire FlatList render (error boundary / red screen), not just one card.
src/screens/admin/AdminStoreLocationsScr.rootCause: Domain type declares `type: 'main'|'branch'|'service'` but the mapper trusts server data blindly; TS can't protect against runtime null from Postgres.
src/screens/admin/AdminStoreLocationsScr.failureScenario: Admin has a store row created by an older schema (or an import) where `type` is NULL. On opening this screen, `renderLocationItem` calls `null.toUpperCase()` and the whole Store Locations screen crashes to the ErrorBoundary. Every subsequent visit crashes until the DB row is fixed.
src/screens/admin/AdminStoreLocationsScr.fix: Guard the call: `{(item.type ? item.type.toUpperCase() : '')} • {item.city}` — or default in the mapper: `type: data.type || 'branch'`.

src/screens/admin/AdminStoreLocationsScr.whatsWrong: `useFocusEffect(useCallback(() => { loadLocations(); }, []))` has an empty dependency array, so the focus callback is frozen to render-1's `loadLocations`, which closes over render-1's `currentAdminId`. If auth hasn't resolved `user` on first render, `currentAdminId` is '' and `loadLocations` early-returns (43-46) setting `loading=false`. When `user` later resolves and `currentAdminId` becomes valid, the frozen effect never re-runs — data never loads.
src/screens/admin/AdminStoreLocationsScr.rootCause: Missing `currentAdminId` in the useCallback dependency array (exhaustive-deps violation); the effect captures a stale admin id.
src/screens/admin/AdminStoreLocationsScr.failureScenario: AuthContext hydrates `user` asynchronously (session read from AsyncStorage). Screen mounts with `user` still null → `currentAdminId=''` → focus effect runs, early-returns, shows the 'No locations' empty state. Auth resolves a moment later but the effect (deps `[]`) never fires again. The admin sees a permanent 'No locations' screen despite owning stores. The empty branch (173-186) has NO RefreshControl, so there is no pull-to-refresh to recover — only a full remount fixes it.
src/screens/admin/AdminStoreLocationsScr.fix: Add the dependency: `useFocusEffect(useCallback(() => { loadLocations(); }, [currentAdminId]))` so the effect re-runs once the admin id becomes available.

src/screens/admin/AdminAnalyticsScreen.t.whatsWrong: fetchData is called from a useEffect keyed on [startDate, endDate, tenantId] with NO request-cancellation or response-ordering guard. Rapid date changes on a slow network fire overlapping requests whose responses resolve out of order, and setData() is applied last-to-RESOLVE, not last-to-FIRE. Worse, the catch branch calls a global Alert.alert (line 66) which fires even after the user has navigated away.
src/screens/admin/AdminAnalyticsScreen.t.rootCause: Async work started in an effect without a cancelled/stale flag or AbortController; the effect returns no cleanup.
src/screens/admin/AdminAnalyticsScreen.t.failureScenario: Admin on slow 3G opens Analytics (3-month range → heavy query starts), then quickly narrows to a 1-week range. The 1-week query returns first and shows correct data; the earlier 3-month query resolves seconds later and overwrites the screen with numbers for the no-longer-selected range. Alternatively the admin taps Back mid-request; the request then fails and an 'Error / No data' Alert pops up on top of whatever screen they navigated to.

src/screens/admin/AdminAnalyticsScreen.t.whatsWrong: The effect calls getAnalyticsData with tenantId unconditionally, including when tenantId is null/undefined (TenantContext not yet resolved). In the service (adminService.ts:454) the tenant filter is applied only `if (tenantId)`, so a null tenantId queries orders/parts across ALL tenants and returns aggregated global revenue/profit — violating GOLDEN_RULES ('never render admin screens without a tenantId; gate on it').
src/screens/admin/AdminAnalyticsScreen.t.rootCause: No tenantId gate before fetching; the service silently degrades to an unfiltered query when tenantId is falsy.
src/screens/admin/AdminAnalyticsScreen.t.failureScenario: Admin opens Analytics before TenantContext finishes resolving (cold start / tenant switch). tenantId is momentarily null, fetchData runs, the Supabase query returns every tenant's delivered orders, and the screen briefly displays total revenue/profit summed across all shops until the effect refires with the resolved tenantId.
src/screens/admin/AdminAnalyticsScreen.t.fix: Gate the fetch: at the top of the effect body add `if (!tenantId) { setData(null); setLoading(false); return; }` (or render a guard/spinner while !tenantId). Also harden the service so a missing tenantId returns `empty` instead of an unfiltered query.

src/screens/admin/AdminConversationsList.whatsWrong: onRefresh only calls setRefreshing(true); it never triggers a data refetch. The list is fed by a realtime subscription set up once in the useEffect (L302-313), and refreshing is reset to false ONLY inside that subscription's callback (L308), which fires exclusively on the initial fetch (already done) and on incoming postgres_changes. So a manual pull sets refreshing=true and nothing ever sets it back.
src/screens/admin/AdminConversationsList.rootCause: Pull-to-refresh state (refreshing) is decoupled from the realtime data source; there is no manual refetch handle and no independent reset path.
src/screens/admin/AdminConversationsList.failureScenario: Admin opens the inbox on a quiet channel (no new messages arriving), pulls down to refresh. The spinner appears and spins forever because no postgres_changes event arrives to invoke the callback that would call setRefreshing(false). The control never dismisses; the admin thinks the app is hung.
src/screens/admin/AdminConversationsList.fix: Since data is already live, either remove the RefreshControl entirely, or release the spinner independently: onRefresh={() => { setRefreshing(true); setTimeout(() => setRefreshing(false), 600); }}. Cleaner: hoist fetchConvs out of the subscription into a useCallback and call it from onRefresh (await it, then setRefreshing(false) in a finally).

src/screens/admin/AdminCreateOrderScreen.whatsWrong: The Create-Sale in-flight guard is state-only. `handleCreate` bails on `if (!tenantId || !lines.length || creating) return` (600) and the button uses `disabled={creating}` (1006), but `creating` is only flipped via `setCreating(true)` (623), which is asynchronous. On a fast double-tap, the second onPress fires from the same committed render — the closure's `creating` is still false and `disabled` still false — so both invocations pass the guard and call `createTenantAdminService(...).createManualOrder(...)` (637). Result: two identical orders, double stock decrement, and double money booked for one walk-in sale (worst on a laggy low-end Android where the commit is slow).
src/screens/admin/AdminCreateOrderScreen.rootCause: The dedupe relies on React state, which does not update synchronously within a single JS tick, so both taps observe the stale pre-submit value.
src/screens/admin/AdminCreateOrderScreen.failureScenario: Admin taps 'Create Sale · $120' twice within ~1 frame. First tap enters handleCreate, schedules setCreating(true) but hasn't re-rendered. Second tap runs the same handleCreate closure (creating still false) and also proceeds. Two orders are created; inventory is decremented twice.
src/screens/admin/AdminCreateOrderScreen.fix: Add a synchronous ref guard: `const creatingRef = useRef(false);` then at the top of handleCreate `if (!tenantId || !lines.length || creatingRef.current) return;`, set `creatingRef.current = true; setCreating(true);` before the await, and in the `finally` block reset both `creatingRef.current = false; setCreating(false);`. Keep `disabled={creating}` for the visual state.

src/screens/admin/AdminCreateOrderScreen.whatsWrong: When `svc.getAllProducts()` (401) rejects — slow/no network, server 500, expired token — the catch only `console.error`s (440) and `finally` sets `loading=false` (442). `products` stays `[]`, so the browse list renders the ListEmptyComponent 'No products found' (718). A network failure is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty catalog and there is no retry affordance, so the admin is stranded and cannot ring up any sale until they kill and relaunch the app.
src/screens/admin/AdminCreateOrderScreen.rootCause: The error path swallows the failure into the same empty state used for a legitimately empty catalog, with no error flag or retry UI.
src/screens/admin/AdminCreateOrderScreen.failureScenario: Store Wi‑Fi drops for 3 seconds while the screen mounts. getAllProducts throws, the spinner disappears, and the admin sees 'No products found' as if the store has zero inventory — with no way to retry short of leaving and re-entering.
src/screens/admin/AdminCreateOrderScreen.fix: Add `const [loadError, setLoadError] = useState(false);`, set `setLoadError(false)` before the fetch and `setLoadError(true)` in the catch. In the catalog area render an error+retry view when `loadError && products.length === 0` (a message plus a TouchableOpacity that re-runs the loader), instead of falling through to the 'No products found' empty component.

src/screens/admin/AdminDiscountsScreen.t.whatsWrong: `{discount.minPurchase && (<View>…</View>)}` (217) and `{discount.minQuantity && (<View>…</View>)}` (226) use `&&` on a numeric field. When the value is exactly 0, `0 && …` short-circuits to the number 0, which React renders as a bare text node. These Views live directly inside `<View style={styles.cardDetails}>` (209), not inside a `<Text>`, so React Native throws the invariant 'Text strings must be rendered within a <Text> component' and the card crashes (caught by App.tsx ErrorBoundary → the entire Discounts list is replaced by the error fallback).
src/screens/admin/AdminDiscountsScreen.t.rootCause: `&&` returns its left operand `0` (a renderable number) instead of a boolean; RN cannot render a stray number outside <Text>.
src/screens/admin/AdminDiscountsScreen.t.failureScenario: Admin creates a discount and types '0' into the optional 'Min Purchase' (or 'Min Items') field → AdminEditDiscountScreen.tsx:184 stores min_purchase = parseFloat('0') = 0 (empty would store NULL, but literal 0 is a natural way to say 'no minimum'). Opening AdminDiscountsScreen, that card evaluates `{0 && …}`, renders the number 0 outside a <Text>, and red-screens / trips the ErrorBoundary for the whole screen. Server/legacy/garbage data returning 0 triggers the same crash.
src/screens/admin/AdminDiscountsScreen.t.fix: Guard against the numeric-0 render with a ternary (which also correctly hides the meaningless 'Min Order: $0' row): `{discount.minPurchase ? (<View>…</View>) : null}` and `{discount.minQuantity ? (<View>…</View>) : null}` — or `{!!discount.minPurchase && (…)}`.

src/screens/admin/AdminDiscountsScreen.t.whatsWrong: onRefresh (65-68) sets `refreshing=true` then calls loadDiscounts, but loadDiscounts' early-return branch when `!tenantId` (38-43) returns at line 42 without ever calling `setRefreshing(false)`. The try/finally that would reset it is never reached, so the RefreshControl spinner spins forever.
src/screens/admin/AdminDiscountsScreen.t.rootCause: Loading/refreshing reset lives only in the happy-path finally, not in the guard clause.
src/screens/admin/AdminDiscountsScreen.t.failureScenario: On an admin session where tenant resolution fails or returns null (tenantLoading=false, tenantId=null) the screen renders the empty state; the admin pulls to refresh → setRefreshing(true) → loadDiscounts hits the early return → refreshing stays true → the pull-to-refresh spinner never stops until the user leaves the screen.
src/screens/admin/AdminDiscountsScreen.t.fix: Reset the flag in the early-return path: in the `!tenantId` branch add `setRefreshing(false)` alongside `setLoading(false)` (e.g. `if (!tenantLoading) { setLoading(false); setRefreshing(false); }`), or restructure so a finally always runs.

src/screens/admin/AdminInboxScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: Each realtime update runs `setConversations(list)` synchronously (ordered, fine) and then fires an un-tracked async `enrichConversationsWithUsers(list).then(setConversations)`. `subscribeToAdminConversations` re-fetches the full list on EVERY postgres change, so two updates in quick succession spawn two overlapping enrich queries whose `.then` callbacks can resolve out of order, letting a stale enriched result clobber newer data.
src/screens/admin/AdminInboxScreen.tsx.rootCause: Async results applied without a latest-wins guard.
src/screens/admin/AdminInboxScreen.tsx.failureScenario: Admin is viewing the inbox on a slow Iraqi network. Update A arrives (5 chats) -> enrich(A) query starts (takes ~1.5s). Before it returns, a customer sends a new message -> update B arrives (6 chats), `setConversations(B)` shows the new chat with its unread badge, enrich(B) starts and resolves fast. Then the slower enrich(A) resolves LAST and calls `setConversations(enrichedA)` -> the UI reverts to 5 chats, and the newest customer conversation + unread count vanish from the admin's inbox until the next unrelated realtime event fires.

src/screens/admin/AdminInvoiceSettingsSc.whatsWrong: A transient network/Supabase failure during getSettings makes the screen render an empty form indistinguishable from a first-time setup. The admin has no signal the load failed. If they fix one field and tap Save, every other field (address, addressAr/Ku, taxId, phone, email, website, logoUrl) is written back as '' — silently overwriting the tenant's real, previously-saved invoice details in the DB.
src/screens/admin/AdminInvoiceSettingsSc.rootCause: The load effect swallows errors: on failure it only calls console.error (L92) and then setLoading(false) (L94), leaving the form fully blank with no user-facing error/retry and no flag distinguishing 'no settings yet' from 'load failed'. handleSave (L129-142) unconditionally writes the ENTIRE settings object built from the empty form state.
src/screens/admin/AdminInvoiceSettingsSc.failureScenario: Iraqi admin on flaky mobile data opens Invoice Settings; getSettings() throws, caught at L91, form shows blank. Admin assumes settings were never entered, types a new company name, taps Save. saveSettings persists {companyName:'NewName', address:'', taxId:'', phone:'', logoUrl:'', ...}, wiping the existing address/tax-id/logo on all future printed invoices.
src/screens/admin/AdminInvoiceSettingsSc.fix: Track load outcome and gate Save: add const [loadError,setLoadError]=useState(false); in catch do { console.error(...); setLoadError(true); } and surface an error+retry UI when loadError. In handleSave, guard: if (loadError) { Alert.alert(t('common.error'), t('admin.invoiceSettings.loadFailedCannotSave', {defaultValue:'Could not load current settings — reload before saving to avoid overwriting data.'})); return; }

src/screens/admin/AdminInvoiceSettingsSc.whatsWrong: Two related defects: (1) If tenantId is never resolved (admin with no tenant), the L59 early-return leaves the full-screen spinner (L184-196) up forever with no empty/error state. (2) If tenantId changes while the screen stays mounted (tenant switcher — the multi-tenant model this app is built around), the effect re-runs but does NOT reset the form; if the new tenant's getSettings returns null the `if (data)` block (L64) is skipped, so the PREVIOUS tenant's companyName/address/logo remain on screen and can be saved under the new tenantId — a cross-tenant data bleed, exactly what GOLDEN_RULES says to prevent (clear tenant state on tenant change). No reload spinner is shown either.
src/screens/admin/AdminInvoiceSettingsSc.rootCause: The loader effect (deps [tenantId]) never sets loading back to true on re-run and never resets form state; it also has no else-branch when data is null. Combined with the early return at L59 when tenantId is falsy, loading (init true, L38) is never set false while tenantId is absent.
src/screens/admin/AdminInvoiceSettingsSc.failureScenario: Admin viewing Tenant A's populated invoice form switches to Tenant B (which has no invoice settings yet). Effect re-runs, getSettings returns null, form still displays Tenant A's company name/address/logo. Admin taps Save and Tenant A's data is written into Tenant B's invoiceSettings.
src/screens/admin/AdminInvoiceSettingsSc.fix: At the top of loadSettings (after the tenant check) call setLoading(true), and always reset the form when there is no data: replace `if (data) { ... }` with an else that clears every field (setCompanyName(''), setAddress(''), setLogoUrl(''), etc.) and reset phone state to defaults. Also handle the absent-tenant case so the spinner can't hang, e.g. `if (!tenantId) { setLoading(false); return; }` (or render an explicit empty/error state).

src/screens/admin/AdminOrdersScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: The QI-Card block is the only place in the entire file that reads selectedOrder.totalUSD WITHOUT the `!= null` guard used at every other total site (628,727,1171,1529,1631,1879,1917,2283...). Line 2130 does `selectedOrder.totalUSD.toFixed(2)` and line 2121 does `Math.round(selectedOrder.totalUSD * (selectedOrder.exchangeRate || 1))`. The type says totalUSD:number, but the file's own pervasive null-guarding proves the Supabase mapping can yield undefined at runtime.
src/screens/admin/AdminOrdersScreen.tsx.rootCause: Missing null-guard on totalUSD inside the qi_card conditional, inconsistent with the rest of the component.
src/screens/admin/AdminOrdersScreen.tsx.failureScenario: Admin opens the detail modal for a qi_card order whose total_usd came back null/undefined (garbage/legacy row). Line 2130 throws `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'selectedOrder.totalUSD.toFixed')`, the modal render crashes into the ErrorBoundary/red screen; line 2121 also renders 'NaN IQD'.

src/screens/admin/AdminOrdersScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: handleMessageCustomer reuses the screen-wide `loading` flag (setLoading(true) at 680). The main render has `if (loading) return <fullscreen spinner>` at 2624, so tapping 'Message Customer' unmounts the open order modal AND the list and replaces the whole screen with a fullscreen spinner until findConversationByTenant/createAdminInitiatedConversation resolve. There is no timeout on those network calls.
src/screens/admin/AdminOrdersScreen.tsx.rootCause: Action-scoped async work driving the global fullscreen `loading` state instead of a dedicated flag.
src/screens/admin/AdminOrdersScreen.tsx.failureScenario: Admin taps 'Message Customer' in the order modal on a slow/stalled connection. The modal vanishes and the entire Orders screen becomes a blank fullscreen spinner with no close/cancel affordance; the admin is stuck until the request finally resolves or rejects. Even on a fast network it produces a jarring full-screen flash before navigating.
src/screens/admin/AdminOrdersScreen.tsx.fix: Add `const [messagingCustomer, setMessagingCustomer] = useState(false);` and use it in handleMessageCustomer instead of setLoading; show an inline spinner on the button (and/or add a request timeout) rather than gating the whole screen.

src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerAssignment.whatsWrong: loadProducts early-returns with `if (!tenantId) return;` (L42) which is BEFORE the try/finally block, so setLoading(false) (in the finally, L58-60) never runs. Combined with the effect that fires as soon as tenantLoading is false (L63-67) and the render gate `if (loading)` (L145), a null/unresolved tenantId leaves the screen stuck on the full-screen ActivityIndicator forever — no error, no empty state, no recovery. This also violates the project's golden rule of gating admin screens on tenantId.
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerAssignment.rootCause: The tenantId guard sits outside the try block, so the only code path that clears the initial `loading=true` is skipped.
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerAssignment.failureScenario: An admin whose tenant fails to resolve (or resolves to null) opens Assign Products. tenantLoading flips to false, loadProducts runs, hits `if (!tenantId) return;`, and the spinner never clears — the screen is permanently frozen and must be force-closed.
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerAssignment.fix: Clear loading before returning: `const loadProducts = useCallback(async () => { if (!tenantId) { setLoading(false); return; } try { ... } finally { setLoading(false); } }, [...])`. Ideally also render an explicit error/empty state when tenantId is missing rather than an infinite spinner.

src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerAssignment.whatsWrong: `if (p.coAdminIds && p.coAdminIds.includes(userId))` calls .includes without confirming coAdminIds is an array. coAdminIds is mapped straight from `extra_data?.coAdminIds` (arbitrary JSON), so a corrupted/legacy row storing it as a number/boolean/object makes `.includes` throw a TypeError. The throw is caught by the surrounding try (so no hard crash), but it aborts the whole pre-selection loop: products were already set (L46) but setSelectedProductIds/setOriginalSelectedIds never run, and the catch fires a misleading 'Failed to load products' alert even though products loaded fine — leaving the owner with a full product list and zero of the partner's existing assignments pre-checked. The service's own setPartnerAssignments guards this exact field with Array.isArray (L1187); this screen does not.
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerAssignment.rootCause: Trusting extra_data.coAdminIds to be an array; inconsistent with the defensive Array.isArray check the service uses.
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerAssignment.failureScenario: One product in the catalog has extra_data.coAdminIds stored as a non-array (manual DB edit / old schema). Opening the assignment screen for any partner throws inside the loop, shows a false error, and drops all pre-existing checkmarks — the owner re-saves and silently wipes that partner's real assignments.

src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerDashboardS.whatsWrong: handleAddMoney has NO synchronous re-entry guard. Its only protection is the Save button's disabled={savingMoney} (626), which takes effect only after a re-render. The handler never checks savingMoney (and could not usefully — the value is captured stale in the render closure). Contrast handleItemPayout (158-186), which the author deliberately protected with savingItemRef. Two fast taps both pass validation and both await addPartnerLedgerEntry, writing the entry twice. Worse: the 'out' payout cap at 112-121 reads realizedProfit-ledgerOut from the same stale closure, so two taps that each individually satisfy the cap can jointly exceed it.
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerDashboardS.rootCause: State-based disable is asynchronous; no ref-based in-flight lock on the write path.
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerDashboardS.failureScenario: Owner opens Add-money, enters 500 'Money in', double-taps Save on a laggy 320dp Android → two +500 deposits recorded → Total Invested inflated by 500. Or with available profit=100, enters 100 'Money out' and double-taps → both pass the cap (each sees ledgerOut before either commits) → 200 paid out against a 100 cap.
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerDashboardS.fix: Add a ref guard mirroring the item-payout pattern: const savingMoneyRef = useRef(false); then at the top of handleAddMoney: if (savingMoneyRef.current) return; set savingMoneyRef.current = true right before setSavingMoney(true) in the try, and reset savingMoneyRef.current = false in the finally alongside setSavingMoney(false).

src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerDashboardS.whatsWrong: parseFloat((moneyAmount||'').replace(/[^0-9.]/g,'')) || 0 strips every character that is not an ASCII 0-9 or dot. Arabic-Indic numerals (٠١٢٣...) and Eastern-Arabic decimals produced by localized numeric keyboards are all removed, yielding amt=0. Line 110 then returns SILENTLY on amt<=0 — the owner gets zero feedback (no 'enter an amount' alert), so the tap appears to do nothing.
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerDashboardS.rootCause: ASCII-only sanitization plus a silent early-return with no validation message.
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerDashboardS.failureScenario: On an ar-IQ/ku device whose numeric keypad emits Arabic-Indic digits, the owner types an amount, taps Save, and nothing happens or is saved — with no error — leaving them unable to record money in the app's primary target locale.
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerDashboardS.fix: Normalize Eastern-Arabic/Persian digits to ASCII before parsing (e.g. map ٠-٩ and ۰-۹ to 0-9, and ٫ to '.'), then if the parsed amount is <=0 show an Alert prompting for a valid amount instead of returning silently.

src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerManagement.whatsWrong: load()'s catch only console.error's — there is no error state. If getPartners() or getAllProducts() rejects (slow/no network, server 500), partners stays [] and setLoading(false) runs, so the FlatList renders ListEmptyComponent 'No Partners Yet / Add a partner…'. A load failure is visually indistinguishable from genuinely having zero partners, with no message and no retry affordance.
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerManagement.rootCause: Only two of three fetches are .catch-guarded (orders is, l.77); partners/products failures fall to a silent console.error with no UI branch.
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerManagement.failureScenario: Owner who has 5 partners opens the screen on a flaky connection; getPartners() throws; they see 'No Partners Yet' and believe their partners were deleted, with no way to retry except leaving and re-entering.
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerManagement.fix: Add `const [error, setError] = useState(false);` set `setError(false)` at the top of load() and `setError(true)` in catch; then render a distinct error+retry view when `error && !partners.length` (an icon, message, and a TouchableOpacity calling load()), separate from the genuine-empty ListEmptyComponent.

src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerManagement.whatsWrong: useFocusEffect(load) returns no cleanup and load() has no cancellation/ignore flag. On tenant change load is recreated (dep tenantId) and re-runs while a prior request may still be in flight; whichever resolves last calls setPartners. Out-of-order resolution can paint a stale (or wrong-tenant) partner list. This also violates the tenant-isolation golden rule (no per-request tenant guard).
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerManagement.rootCause: Fire-and-forget async in the focus effect with a shared setState and no request-generation guard.
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerManagement.failureScenario: Owner switches tenant (or rapidly backs out and re-enters); tenant A's slow getPartners resolves after tenant B's, so the screen briefly shows tenant A's partners under tenant B.
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerManagement.fix: Guard the effect: `useFocusEffect(useCallback(() => { let active = true; (async () => { /* fetch */ if (active) setPartners(withStats); if (active) setLoading(false); })(); return () => { active = false; }; }, [tenantId]));` (capture tenantId in the closure and drop results when inactive).

src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerManagement.whatsWrong: load() starts with `if (!tenantId) return;` BEFORE the try/finally, so this early return never runs setLoading(false). loading is initialized true (l.60). If tenantId is null on first focus and never becomes truthy (tenant resolution failed for this owner), the screen is stuck on the full-screen ActivityIndicator forever with no timeout or error path.
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerManagement.rootCause: Early bailout placed outside the finally block that owns setLoading(false).
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerManagement.failureScenario: Owner whose TenantContext fails to resolve a tenantId opens Partner Management and sees an infinite spinner with no error or retry.
src/screens/admin/AdminPartnerManagement.fix: Clear the flag on the guard: `if (!tenantId) { setLoading(false); return; }` — and pair with the error-state UI from the load-error finding so an unresolved tenant surfaces a message instead of a permanent spinner.

src/screens/admin/AdminProductsScreen.ts.whatsWrong: Bulk status-update and bulk-delete map each server call through `.catch(() => {})`, so every per-item rejection is swallowed. Promise.all then always RESOLVES, so the surrounding `try/catch { Alert(bulkFailed) }` is dead code — it can never fire. Immediately after, the code optimistically rewrites local state (setProducts prev.map / prev.filter) and clears the selection.
src/screens/admin/AdminProductsScreen.ts.rootCause: Per-item `.catch(()=>{})` hides failures AND the optimistic local update is never reconciled with actual server results.
src/screens/admin/AdminProductsScreen.ts.failureScenario: Admin selects 20 products, taps 'Available' (or delete) with no/slow network. All 20 updateProduct/deleteProduct calls reject, each swallowed. Promise.all resolves, local list flips all 20 to Available (or removes them), selection bar closes, NO error is shown — looks 100% successful. On the next pull-to-refresh / screen focus, loadProducts overwrites with server truth and every change is gone. Silent data loss disguised as success.
src/screens/admin/AdminProductsScreen.ts.fix: Use allSettled and reconcile: `const results = await Promise.allSettled(ids.map(id => service.updateProduct(id,{status}))); const failed = results.filter(r=>r.status==='rejected').length; setSelectionMode(false); setSelectedIds(new Set()); await loadProducts(); if (failed) Alert.alert(t('admin.common.error'), t('admin.products.bulkFailed'));` — drop the optimistic prev.map/prev.filter and the now-unreachable outer catch. Same for bulkDelete.

src/screens/admin/AdminProductsScreen.ts.whatsWrong: The wholesale price-tier list is keyed by array index (`key={index}`, line 2320) while the PRICE field is UNCONTROLLED (`defaultValue={tier.priceUSD...}`, line 2361 — it only commits on onEndEditing). minQty/maxQty are controlled `value=` so they update, but the uncontrolled price input keeps whatever it mounted with. Deleting a tier (line 2380 filters by index) shifts every later tier up one index, and React reuses the existing input node for that key.
src/screens/admin/AdminProductsScreen.ts.rootCause: Uncontrolled defaultValue + index-as-key: React can't reset an uncontrolled input when the item behind a reused key changes.
src/screens/admin/AdminProductsScreen.ts.failureScenario: Three tiers: (min5,$10),(min10,$20),(min15,$30). Admin deletes the first row. State correctly becomes [(min10,$20),(min15,$30)] and the controlled minQty fields show 10 and 15 — but the two price inputs (key 0 and 1, uncontrolled) keep their original mounted text and still display $10 and $20. Admin now sees 'min10 → $10, min15 → $20', a silent mismatch between the shown price and the value that will be saved. Any subsequent edit/save persists the wrong (still-old-state) prices.
src/screens/admin/AdminProductsScreen.ts.fix: Give each tier a stable id at creation (`{ id: `tier_${Date.now()}`, minQty, priceUSD:0 }`) and use `key={tier.id}`; OR make the price input controlled: `value={tier.priceUSD ? String(tier.priceUSD) : ''}` with onChangeText updating state (parse on blur if you want). Do not combine defaultValue with index keys on a removable list.

src/screens/admin/AdminProductsScreen.ts.whatsWrong: loadProducts does not verify the response still belongs to the current tenant before calling setProducts, and there is no in-flight/abort guard. The tenant-change reset effect (179-202) clears products but also does NOT clear selection state (selectedIds/selectionMode), sortMode, or managedCategories — contradicting the CLAUDE.md rule 'clear all tenant state on tenant change'.
src/screens/admin/AdminProductsScreen.ts.rootCause: No request-token/tenant check on async completion; incomplete state reset on tenant change.
src/screens/admin/AdminProductsScreen.ts.failureScenario: Admin owning two shops switches tenant A→B quickly. loadProducts(A) is still in flight; the reset effect clears the list and loadProducts(B) starts. If A's response arrives after B's, setProducts(A-data) runs last and tenant B's screen now renders tenant A's products (keyExtractor stamps them 'B-<A.id>'). Separately, if a multi-select was active during the switch, selectedIds still holds tenant-A ids and a bulk action fires updateProduct against tenant B's service on foreign ids.
src/screens/admin/AdminProductsScreen.ts.fix: Capture the tenant at call time and bail on completion if it changed: `const reqTenant = tenantId; const data = await service.getAllProducts(); if (reqTenant !== tenantId) return; setProducts(...)` (read current tenant via a ref to avoid stale closure). Also add `setSelectionMode(false); setSelectedIds(new Set()); setSortMode('default'); setManagedCategories([]);` to the tenantId reset effect.

src/screens/admin/AdminProductsScreen.ts.whatsWrong: Multiple direct mutations of state. Line 549: `priceTiers.sort((a,b)=>a.minQty-b.minQty).map(...)` sorts the state array IN PLACE (Array.sort mutates). Lines 2327-2366: `const newTiers = [...priceTiers]` is only a shallow copy, so `newTiers[index].minQty = ...` mutates the very same tier object held in state (and, since tiers come from `product.priceTiers` at line 433, it also mutates editingProduct.priceTiers).
src/screens/admin/AdminProductsScreen.ts.rootCause: Mutating arrays/objects that are React state instead of producing new copies.
src/screens/admin/AdminProductsScreen.ts.failureScenario: Line 549: on a save that then FAILS (catch at 633 shows saveFailed, resetForm is NOT called), the still-open modal's tier rows have been silently reordered under the user because the backing state array was sorted in place. Lines 2328/2366: editing a tier's qty/price mutates the shared object that editingProduct still points at, so a later comparison against 'original' product data (e.g. duplicate detection or a re-open) sees the already-edited values, not the originals.
src/screens/admin/AdminProductsScreen.ts.fix: Line 549: sort a copy — `[...priceTiers].sort(...)`. Lines 2327-2366: replace element-mutation with immutable update, e.g. `setPriceTiers(prev => prev.map((tr,i) => i===index ? { ...tr, minQty: parseInt(text,10)||0 } : tr))` (same pattern for maxQty and priceUSD).

src/screens/admin/AdminSignupScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: During an in-flight request the primary button is disabled (disabled={loading}) but the Back button (line 146) and the Cancel link (line 234) both call handleBack -> navigation.goBack() with no guard. If the user taps Cancel/Back while isPhoneRegistered / supabase.auth.signInWithOtp is still awaiting, the screen pops and unmounts; when the promise later resolves it runs navigation.navigate('VerifyPhone'/'AdminVerifyEmail', ...) (lines 90/121) plus setState in finally, force-navigating the user FORWARD into a verify screen they just abandoned (and a setState-after-unmount warning).
src/screens/admin/AdminSignupScreen.tsx.rootCause: No mounted/aborted guard before the post-await navigate, and secondary dismiss controls are not disabled while loading.
src/screens/admin/AdminSignupScreen.tsx.failureScenario: Slow Iraqi 3G: admin taps 'Send code', waits ~2s, gives up and taps Cancel -> returns to previous screen. ~1s later signInWithOtp resolves and the app abruptly jumps to AdminVerifyEmail asking for an OTP the user never wanted.
src/screens/admin/AdminSignupScreen.tsx.fix: Add a mounted ref: `const aliveRef = useRef(true); useEffect(() => () => { aliveRef.current = false; }, []);` and gate both navigates with `if (!aliveRef.current) return;` before navigation.navigate(...). Additionally set `disabled={loading}` on the Back TouchableOpacity (line 146) and Cancel TouchableOpacity (line 234) so they can't fire mid-request.

src/screens/admin/AdminSignupScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: handleSendCode has no synchronous re-entrancy guard; it relies solely on disabled={loading}, which only takes effect after React commits the re-render. Because setLoading(true) is followed by an await, a fast double-tap can dispatch a second onPress before the disabled prop is committed, running the request twice. In the email branch this calls supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ shouldCreateUser:true }) twice -> two OTP emails and a duplicate create attempt.
src/screens/admin/AdminSignupScreen.tsx.rootCause: State-driven disable (disabled={loading}) has an unavoidable commit-race window; there is no imperative ref latch.
src/screens/admin/AdminSignupScreen.tsx.failureScenario: User double-taps 'Continue' on the email tab within ~50ms; both taps pass the disabled check, two signInWithOtp calls fire, the user gets two 6-digit codes and is confused which to enter.
src/screens/admin/AdminSignupScreen.tsx.fix: Add `const submittingRef = useRef(false);` then at the top of handleSendCode: `if (submittingRef.current) return; submittingRef.current = true;` and reset it in a try/finally (`finally { submittingRef.current = false; }`) wrapping the whole body.

src/screens/admin/AdminStoreProfileScree.whatsWrong: useFocusEffect calls loadData() on EVERY focus, and loadData unconditionally does setProfile(existingProfile) plus re-parses phone/whatsapp state, overwriting all unsaved edits. There is no dirty check and no in-flight cancellation, so two rapid focus/blur cycles can also race.
src/screens/admin/AdminStoreProfileScree.rootCause: The screen treats focus as 'always refetch and replace local state', but local state here is an in-progress edit form, not read-only data.
src/screens/admin/AdminStoreProfileScree.failureScenario: Admin fills in Store Name, About, social links and store hours, then (still on this screen) opens the Location picker and taps 'Add Location' (line 1177) which navigates to AdminEditStoreLocation. On returning, the screen refocuses -> loadData runs -> setProfile(existingProfile) resets every field to the server version. All unsaved edits are silently wiped.
src/screens/admin/AdminStoreProfileScree.fix: Only hydrate the form the first time, and on subsequent focuses refresh just the locations list. e.g. const didLoad = useRef(false); in loadData guard the profile hydration with `if (!didLoad.current) { setProfile(existingProfile); ...parse phones...; didLoad.current = true; }` while always refreshing `setLocations(activeLocations)`. Alternatively track a `dirty` flag and skip re-hydration when dirty, prompting the user instead.

src/screens/admin/AdminStoreProfileScree.whatsWrong: The DateTimePicker `value` is built from `new Date(new Date().setHours(parseInt(profile.openTime.split(':')[0]), parseInt(profile.openTime.split(':')[1])))` with no validation and no radix. A non-'HH:MM' string produces NaN -> Invalid Date, which the iOS inline spinner receives as its `value`.
src/screens/admin/AdminStoreProfileScree.rootCause: `profile.openTime ?` only checks truthiness, not shape, and the render trusts server data to always be well-formed 'HH:MM'.
src/screens/admin/AdminStoreProfileScree.failureScenario: Server/DB returns openTime like '8' (no colon) or 'closed'. useCustomHours becomes true (non-null), so on iOS the inline DateTimePicker renders with value = Invalid Date (split(':')[1] is undefined -> parseInt(undefined) = NaN -> setHours(8, NaN)). The native iOS date picker can throw/misbehave on an Invalid Date, blanking or crashing the Store Hours section.
src/screens/admin/AdminStoreProfileScree.fix: Parse defensively: `const parseHHMM = (s?: string): Date => { const m = /^(\d{2}):(\d{2})$/.exec(s ?? ''); const d = new Date(); if (m) d.setHours(parseInt(m[1],10), parseInt(m[2],10), 0, 0); else d.setHours(8,0,0,0); return d; };` and use parseHHMM(profile.openTime)/parseHHMM(profile.closeTime) in all four picker `value` props. Always pass radix 10.

src/screens/admin/AdminSuccessScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: handleEnterDashboard does `await refreshUser()` BEFORE calling navigation.reset, so leaving the screen is gated behind a network call. There is also no in-flight guard, and the useEffect (lines 74-77) already refreshes auth in the background, making this await redundant.
src/screens/admin/AdminSuccessScreen.tsx.rootCause: Awaiting a network side-effect on the primary navigation action instead of firing it in the background and navigating immediately.
src/screens/admin/AdminSuccessScreen.tsx.failureScenario: On slow/no network (very common in Iraq target market), the admin taps 'Enter dashboard' at the end of store setup. refreshUser() hangs or takes 20-30s (no visible timeout guarantee); the button shows no spinner and is not disabled, so it looks dead. The user cannot leave the success screen until the request resolves — and if refreshUser never resolves, they are permanently stuck. Impatient double/triple-tapping queues multiple refreshUser() calls and multiple navigation.reset('Main') dispatches (the second fires from an already-unmounted screen).

src/screens/admin/AdminVerifyEmailScreen.whatsWrong: handleVerify() has no in-flight guard. The Confirm button's `disabled={loading}` (239) only takes effect after the loading state commits and re-renders; two rapid taps within the same frame both see disabled=false and both invoke handleVerify. There is also a second entry path: typing/pasting the 6th digit auto-submits via handleVerify(newCode) (100,116) — a user who taps Confirm at the same instant the auto-submit fires triggers two concurrent supabase.auth.verifyOtp calls. The first consumes the OTP and runs navigation.navigate('AdminStoreName'); the second races to push/navigate the next screen again and/or fires a duplicate verify with an already-consumed token.
src/screens/admin/AdminVerifyEmailScreen.rootCause: No boolean/ref re-entrancy guard at the top of the async submit handler; the only guard is a derived `disabled` prop that updates asynchronously.
src/screens/admin/AdminVerifyEmailScreen.failureScenario: On a 320dp low-RAM Android under load, the user pastes the code (auto-submit fires) and also taps Confirm before the row re-renders. Two verifyOtp requests go out; AdminStoreName gets navigated to twice (duplicate screen in the stack) and the second verify errors on the consumed token, momentarily flashing an error before/after the transition.
src/screens/admin/AdminVerifyEmailScreen.fix: Add a re-entrancy guard as the first line of handleVerify: `if (loading) return;` (before building otpCode at 130). Mirror it in handleResend: add `if (resending) return;` alongside the existing `if (cooldown > 0) return;` at line 165.

src/screens/admin/AdminBannerScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: handleToggleActive computes the network target from the render-closure value (!banner.isActive) but updates local state with a RELATIVE flip in the functional updater (b.id===banner.id ? {...b, isActive: !b.isActive}). There is no in-flight guard. On a slow network these two disagree when the Switch is tapped twice before the first await resolves.
src/screens/admin/AdminBannerScreen.tsx.rootCause: Local optimistic state uses a relative toggle (!b.isActive) instead of the absolute target sent to the server; both taps capture the same stale `banner.isActive` for the request.
src/screens/admin/AdminBannerScreen.tsx.failureScenario: Banner is Active (true). On a slow connection the admin taps the Switch twice quickly. Both calls send updateBanner(id,{isActive:false}) so the DB ends up false (correct). But the two success callbacks each flip prev state: first true→false (correct), second false→true. Final UI shows Active=true while the DB says inactive — the switch now lies until a manual reload.

src/screens/admin/AdminBrandManagerScree.whatsWrong: The Add/Edit Modal is a bottom-anchored sheet (modalOverlay justifyContent:'flex-end') containing the brand-name TextInput (167-173) and the Save/Cancel buttons (180-187), but there is NO KeyboardAvoidingView. When the name input is focused the software keyboard slides over the bottom of the screen and covers the input itself plus the Save/Cancel row, because the sheet is pinned to the bottom and its content sits within ~260px of the bottom edge.
src/screens/admin/AdminBrandManagerScree.rootCause: Modal content is not wrapped in a KeyboardAvoidingView, and RN Modal does not auto-adjust for the keyboard (especially transparent modals on iOS).
src/screens/admin/AdminBrandManagerScree.failureScenario: Admin taps + to add a brand, taps the name field to type 'Samsung'. On iOS (which never auto-avoids the keyboard) and on small-screen / max-font Android, the ~330px keyboard covers the name field AND the Save button. The admin cannot see what they type and cannot reach Save without first dismissing the keyboard — the add-brand flow is effectively blocked on those devices.
src/screens/admin/AdminBrandManagerScree.fix: Import { KeyboardAvoidingView, Platform } from 'react-native' and wrap the sheet: replace `<View style={styles.modalOverlay}>` with `<KeyboardAvoidingView behavior={Platform.OS === 'ios' ? 'padding' : 'height'} style={styles.modalOverlay}>` (and close with </KeyboardAvoidingView>), keeping the inner modalCard View. This lifts the sheet above the keyboard so the input and Save button stay visible.

src/screens/admin/AdminBusinessInfoScree.whatsWrong: The effect calls fetchBusinessInfo() with no cancellation/ignore flag and no cleanup. Two fetches can be in flight at once and the later-resolving one wins (out-of-order). This is not hypothetical: TenantContext initializes tenantId to null (TenantContext.tsx:69) and sets it asynchronously after session resolves, so on mount the effect commonly fires first with tenantId=null (taking the `!tenantId` global-settings branch, line 116-135) and again when the real tenantId arrives (tenant branch, 81-111). If the global-settings response resolves last, the tenant's form is populated with GLOBAL business info. On a tenant switch A->B, if A's response lands after B's, formData holds tenant A's data while tenantId===B.
src/screens/admin/AdminBusinessInfoScree.rootCause: useEffect performs an async fetch keyed on tenantId but never guards against stale responses or unmount; setState is called unconditionally when the promise resolves.
src/screens/admin/AdminBusinessInfoScree.failureScenario: Admin switches from tenant A to tenant B; B's row loads fast, A's slow response arrives afterward and overwrites the form with A's name/phone/email. Admin taps Save: handleSave (173-176) updates the row for the CURRENT tenantId (B) using the stale formData from A -> tenant A's business info is written into tenant B's row (cross-tenant data corruption). Same class of bug also flashes global settings over tenant data on first mount.

src/screens/admin/AdminCategoriesScreen..whatsWrong: save() has no in-flight guard at function entry. The only protection is disabled={saving} on the Save button, but setSaving(true) is asynchronous — the disabled prop only reaches the native button after the next render. Adding `if (saving) return` would not fully fix it either, because the onPress closure captures a stale `saving` value from the last render.
src/screens/admin/AdminCategoriesScreen..rootCause: In-flight state used for a guard lags a render; no synchronous ref latch.
src/screens/admin/AdminCategoriesScreen..failureScenario: On a low-RAM Android device with a busy JS thread, the admin double-taps Save fast. Both onPress events fire before React re-renders and disables the button; each call reads the pre-render state and proceeds, so svc.addCategory(form) runs twice -> two identical categories are created in the tenant.
src/screens/admin/AdminCategoriesScreen..fix: Add a ref latch: `const savingRef = useRef(false);` then at the top of save(): `if (savingRef.current) return; savingRef.current = true;` set it before setSaving(true), and reset `savingRef.current = false;` in the finally block alongside setSaving(false).

src/screens/admin/AdminCategoriesScreen..whatsWrong: pickIcon uses try/finally with NO catch. The finally resets uploading (so no infinite spinner), but if ImageService.showImagePicker() or ImageService.uploadImage() THROWS (network failure, permission error, native picker error), the else-branch Alert is never reached, the user gets no feedback, and the rejected promise escapes an onPress (fire-and-forget) call as an unhandled promise rejection.
src/screens/admin/AdminCategoriesScreen..rootCause: No catch clause to surface thrown errors from the picker/upload.
src/screens/admin/AdminCategoriesScreen..failureScenario: Admin on a weak connection taps 'Upload icon', picks a photo; uploadImage() rejects mid-request (timeout/DNS). The spinner stops but no error dialog appears — the admin thinks nothing happened and no image was set, with an unhandled rejection logged.
src/screens/admin/AdminCategoriesScreen..fix: Add a catch before finally: `} catch { Alert.alert(t('common.error','Error'), t('admin.categories.uploadError','Upload failed')); } finally { setUploading(false); }`

src/screens/admin/AdminCategoryManagerSc.whatsWrong: load() does `setItems(await categoryStore.getAll()); setLoading(false);` with no try/catch, and useEffect fires it as a floating promise (line 46). There is no error state and setLoading(false) only runs on the happy path. If getAll() ever rejects, loading stays true forever and the screen is a permanent spinner with no retry, plus an unhandled promise rejection.
src/screens/admin/AdminCategoryManagerSc.rootCause: Async loader flips the loading flag only in the success branch; no catch/finally and no error UI, so any rejection wedges the screen.
src/screens/admin/AdminCategoryManagerSc.failureScenario: AsyncStorage @asankary_categories_mock_v1 holds valid-JSON-but-non-array content (e.g. "null" or "{}" written by a bad migration/older build). readMock() returns that non-array, categoryStore.getAll() calls .sort() on it (categoryStore.ts line 53) and throws, load() rejects, setLoading(false) never runs -> the Categories manager is stuck on the loading spinner every launch with no way to recover in-app.
src/screens/admin/AdminCategoryManagerSc.fix: const load = useCallback(async () => { try { setItems(await categoryStore.getAll()); } catch (e) { setItems([]); } finally { setLoading(false); } }, []); (optionally surface an error/retry state instead of silently showing empty).

src/screens/admin/AdminChangePasswordScr.whatsWrong: Line 60 checks `error.message.includes('auth/wrong-password')` — a Firebase auth error code. But AuthService.changePassword is Supabase-backed and throws `new Error('Current password is incorrect')` on a bad current password (authService.ts:241 and :249), and `new Error('Not signed in')` / `'Cannot verify current password'` otherwise. The Firebase code string is NEVER produced anywhere in the Supabase path, so the wrong-password branch is dead code. Every failure falls to line 63, which shows the raw English `error.message` directly. English users happen to see acceptable text (en.json wrongPassword is coincidentally the same literal English), but Arabic (ar) and Kurdish (ku) admins — the actual target audience — get raw English error strings instead of the localized `admin.changePassword.wrongPassword` / `failed` messages.
src/screens/admin/AdminChangePasswordScr.rootCause: Error-matching logic copied from the old Firebase flow was never updated for the Supabase backend, which produces different error message strings.
src/screens/admin/AdminChangePasswordScr.failureScenario: An Arabic-locale admin types the wrong current password and taps Update. AuthService throws Error('Current password is incorrect'). Line 60 is false (no 'auth/wrong-password' substring), so line 63 pops an Alert reading the English 'Current password is incorrect' inside an otherwise-Arabic UI. The translated wrongPassword string never renders.

src/screens/admin/AdminCurrencySettingsS.whatsWrong: The rate Input uses keyboardType="numeric", which on iOS exposes a decimal-point (".") key, but onChangeText strips every non-digit via text.replace(/[^0-9]/g,'') and then parseInt. A decimal is not rejected — its dot is deleted and the surrounding digits are concatenated. Typing the plausible rate "1310.5" yields "13105" -> parseInt = 13105, a ~10x-inflated exchange rate. There is no upper/lower bound check, and because CurrencyContext.applyRate accepts any value >0 (CurrencyContext.tsx L47-53) and rebroadcasts it over a realtime postgres_changes channel (L69), the garbage rate propagates live to EVERY buyer's prices instantly (convertUSDToIQD multiplies by rate, so all IQD prices jump ~10x).
src/screens/admin/AdminCurrencySettingsS.rootCause: Numeric keyboard advertises decimals to the user, but the sanitizer removes the decimal separator and concatenates digits instead of rejecting/parsing them, and there is no sane-range clamp before the value goes live.
src/screens/admin/AdminCurrencySettingsS.failureScenario: Admin on iOS edits the USD->IQD rate and types '1310.5' (or fat-fingers a stray '.'), the field shows a value, Save succeeds, and within seconds every product/cart/order price shown to all buyers is multiplied by 13105 instead of 1310.5 — roughly 10x too high — with no validation catching it.
src/screens/admin/AdminCurrencySettingsS.fix: Use keyboardType="number-pad" (integer keypad, no decimal key) and validate/clamp on save. E.g. in onChangeText keep the digit strip, and in handleSave add a guard: `if (exchangeRateIQD === undefined || exchangeRateIQD < 100 || exchangeRateIQD > 100000) { Alert.alert(t('admin.common.error'), t('admin.currency.invalidRate')); return; }` before setSaving(true).

src/screens/admin/AdminCurrencySettingsS.whatsWrong: handleSave performs no validation. If exchangeRateIQD is undefined (empty field) or 0, line 64 computes `exchangeRateIQD || undefined` = undefined and passes exchangeRateIQD: undefined to updateBusinessInfo. That undefined overwrites the existing numeric rate in the merged object (settingsService L21) and, because JSON serialization drops undefined keys, the previously-stored exchangeRateIQD is DELETED from global_settings. The user still gets the 'Success' alert (L67) and goBack (L68). Live prices don't change immediately (CurrencyContext.applyRate ignores non->0 values), so the corruption is invisible until the next cold start / cache miss, when every buyer silently reverts from the admin's configured rate to the hardcoded 1500 fallback (CurrencyContext.tsx L21) — a large, unannounced price shift across the whole store.
src/screens/admin/AdminCurrencySettingsS.rootCause: No guard rejecting an empty/zero rate before save, combined with `x || undefined` turning a missing value into an explicit key-deletion that a 'Success' toast masks.
src/screens/admin/AdminCurrencySettingsS.failureScenario: Admin opens the screen on a slow network so fetchSettings fails and the field renders empty (or the admin clears the field to retype and is interrupted), taps Save, sees 'Success', and leaves. The stored exchange rate is now deleted; on the next app cold start all buyers' IQD prices jump to the 1500 default rate.
src/screens/admin/AdminCurrencySettingsS.fix: Reject empty/invalid input before saving: `if (exchangeRateIQD === undefined || exchangeRateIQD <= 0) { Alert.alert(t('admin.common.error'), t('admin.currency.invalidRate')); return; }` at the top of handleSave, and send `exchangeRateIQD` directly (drop the `|| undefined`) so a valid number is persisted as-is.

src/screens/admin/AdminCustomersScreen.t.whatsWrong: handleOpenInMaps builds the URL by string-interpolating the raw address title and calls Linking.openURL with no .catch. The title is an untrusted user string (Address.title is a free-text field, often Arabic with spaces, e.g. "بيت العائلة" or "Home Office"). Interpolated unencoded into `maps:0,0?q=${title}@lat,lng` / `geo:0,0?q=lat,lng(${title})`, a space or an '@'/'&' in the title produces a malformed URL that drops the pin at the wrong place or fails to parse. Separately, Linking.openURL returns a promise that REJECTS when no app can handle the scheme (e.g. an AOSP/Huawei Android device with no Google Maps for the geo: scheme). With no .catch, that becomes an unhandled promise rejection.
src/screens/admin/AdminCustomersScreen.t.rootCause: Missing encodeURIComponent on user input and missing .catch on a promise-returning native call.
src/screens/admin/AdminCustomersScreen.t.failureScenario: Admin opens a customer address titled 'Home Office' and taps 'Open in Maps' on an Android device without Google Maps installed: the geo: intent has no handler, openURL rejects, and the rejection is unhandled (dev red-box / silent failure in prod) with no user feedback. On a device that does open maps, the unencoded space in the title yields a garbled q-parameter.

src/screens/admin/AdminEditStoreLocation.whatsWrong: The ownership guard `if (location.createdByAdminId && location.createdByAdminId !== currentAdminId)` compares against `currentAdminId = user?.uid || ''` captured in the loadLocation closure. The effect deps are `[locationId]` only, so if the screen mounts before AuthContext has rehydrated `user` (cold start / re-mount / deep link into edit), `currentAdminId` is '' at capture time. Since a real location always has a `createdByAdminId`, the condition becomes `'nonEmpty' !== ''` → true.
src/screens/admin/AdminEditStoreLocation.rootCause: currentAdminId is read from a stale closure and the effect never re-runs when user finishes loading.
src/screens/admin/AdminEditStoreLocation.failureScenario: Legitimate owner opens 'Edit' on their own store location during a slow auth restore → sees 'You do not have permission to edit this location' and is bounced back with navigation.goBack(). They can never edit their own location until auth happens to be warm.
src/screens/admin/AdminEditStoreLocation.fix: Defer the load until the admin id is known and re-run when it arrives: `useEffect(() => { if (isEditing && locationId && currentAdminId) loadLocation(); }, [locationId, currentAdminId]);` and additionally harden the check to `if (location.createdByAdminId && currentAdminId && location.createdByAdminId !== currentAdminId)`.

src/screens/admin/AdminEditStoreLocation.whatsWrong: `openTimePicker` (L268) — the only place `setShowTimePicker(true)` is called — is never invoked from the JSX.
