src/screens/admin/AdminEditStoreLocation.rootCause: The working-hours editor UI that would call openTimePicker was removed/never rendered while its supporting code and default state were left in.
src/screens/admin/AdminEditStoreLocation.failureScenario: Admin creates or edits any store location. They have no control to set opening hours, and every location is silently persisted with Sunday-Saturday 09:00-18:00, isOpen:true for all 7 days — including Friday (the Iraqi weekend). Customers then see incorrect store hours with no way for the admin to correct them.
src/screens/admin/AdminEditStoreLocation.fix: Either render a working-hours section whose time buttons call openTimePicker(day, field) so the existing picker/handlers are actually used, or if hours are intentionally out of scope, remove the dead state/handlers/modal (L87,101-102,261-300,518-553) and stop sending `workingHours` in locationData.

src/screens/admin/AdminEditStoreLocation.whatsWrong: loadLocation sets required fields with no fallback: `setName(location.name)`, `setAddress(location.address)`, `setCity(location.city)`. mapDbToLocation (locationService L144,147,152) passes `data.name`/`data.address`/`data.city` straight through with no defaulting, so a null/garbage DB row yields null state. handleSave then calls `name.trim()`, `address.trim()`, `city.trim()` (L211).
src/screens/admin/AdminEditStoreLocation.rootCause: Server values assumed non-null; neither the mapper nor the setters coerce to string.
src/screens/admin/AdminEditStoreLocation.failureScenario: A legacy/corrupt store_locations row has name=null. Admin opens it, changes only the phone, taps Save → `!name.trim()` throws 'Cannot read property trim of null' (TypeError) and the save handler crashes instead of showing the required-fields alert.
src/screens/admin/AdminEditStoreLocation.fix: Coerce on load: `setName(location.name || ''); setAddress(location.address || ''); setCity(location.city || '');` (or default these in mapDbToLocation).

src/screens/admin/AdminPromoManagerScree.whatsWrong: The Add/Edit modal is a bottom-anchored sheet (modalOverlay justifyContent:'flex-end') containing three TextInputs, a Switch, and the Save button, with NO KeyboardAvoidingView and NO ScrollView. This violates the CLAUDE.md keyboard rule (SafeAreaView → KeyboardAvoidingView → ScrollView). When the soft keyboard opens for the last field (Min purchase, line 192), it covers that input, the Active switch (201-204), and the Save/Cancel buttons (206-213). With max OS font size or Arabic/Kurdish RTL on a 320dp screen the fixed-height card can also grow past the top of the screen with no way to scroll to the Code field or title.
src/screens/admin/AdminPromoManagerScree.rootCause: Modal body is a plain <View> with no keyboard avoidance or scroll owner.
src/screens/admin/AdminPromoManagerScree.failureScenario: Admin on a 320dp Android taps a promo to edit, taps 'Min purchase', the numeric keyboard slides up and hides the field being typed AND the Save button. They cannot see what they type or submit without dismissing the keyboard first; on a small screen the Code field at top is also unreachable.
src/screens/admin/AdminPromoManagerScree.fix:
Wrap the modal card in KeyboardAvoidingView and make the fields a scroll owner, e.g.:
<KeyboardAvoidingView behavior={Platform.OS === 'ios' ? 'padding' : undefined} style={styles.modalOverlay}>
  <ScrollView keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled" contentContainerStyle={{ flexGrow: 1, justifyContent: 'flex-end' }}>
    <View style={[styles.modalCard, ...]}>...</View>
  </ScrollView>
</KeyboardAvoidingView>
(import Platform, KeyboardAvoidingView, ScrollView from react-native).

src/screens/admin/AdminPromoManagerScree.whatsWrong: Both numeric fields are controlled by a value derived from Number(): value={form.value != null ? String(form.value) : ''} with onChangeText v => setForm({ value: v === '' ? undefined : Number(v) }) (lines 183-184; same for minPurchase 193-194). Because Number('5.') === 5, typing a decimal point is immediately stripped by the re-render, so an admin can never enter a decimal (e.g. 5.5% or a $29.99 min purchase / cents). Worse, if any non-numeric text reaches the field (paste, or Android numeric keyboards that permit commas/letters), Number(...) yields NaN and value={String(NaN)} renders the literal string 'NaN' in the input.
src/screens/admin/AdminPromoManagerScree.rootCause: Controlled input value is round-tripped through Number()/String() on every keystroke instead of holding the raw text.
src/screens/admin/AdminPromoManagerScree.failureScenario: Admin creates a 'SAVE10' code and types '5.5' in Amount off: after '5' then '.', the field snaps back to '5' and the dot vanishes — decimals are impossible. Separately, pasting 'abc' into the field makes it display 'NaN' and Save is blocked (value<=0) with no explanation.
src/screens/admin/AdminPromoManagerScree.fix: Hold the raw text in state (e.g. keep form.value as a string, or add valueText/minText string state), sanitize to digits+one dot, and parse once in save(): const value = Number((form.valueText || '').replace(',', '.')); Only convert to a number at submit, never in onChangeText. This preserves partial input like '5.' and never shows 'NaN'.

src/screens/admin/AdminPromoManagerScree.whatsWrong: save() awaits promoService.save() inside try/finally with NO catch (lines 65-80). promoService.writeMock deliberately lets AsyncStorage.setItem rejections propagate (its comment: 'so save()/remove() callers can surface them') — but this caller does not surface anything. On a write failure the exception escapes the async save() as an unhandled promise rejection, setModalVisible(false) is skipped, and the user gets no error Alert — the modal just sits there with no feedback. remove() (line 92: onPress: async () => { await promoService.remove(p.id); await load(); }) has the same missing catch. load() (39-43) also has no catch and no finally: today mock getAll() can't reject, but the moment the TODO(live) Supabase read is wired, any error leaves setLoading(false) unreached → permanent spinner.
src/screens/admin/AdminPromoManagerScree.rootCause: Async service calls are not wrapped in try/catch that alerts the user, and load() sets loading=false only on the success path.
src/screens/admin/AdminPromoManagerScree.failureScenario: On a device with a full disk, admin edits a promo and taps Save: AsyncStorage.setItem rejects, save() throws, the modal stays open with no error message and the change is silently lost (unhandled rejection). Later, once Supabase is wired, a network failure on load leaves the screen stuck on the ActivityIndicator forever.
src/screens/admin/AdminPromoManagerScree.fix: Add catch blocks that surface the error: in save() add `catch (e) { Alert.alert(t('common.error',{defaultValue:'Error'}), t('admin.promos.saveFailed',{defaultValue:'Could not save. Try again.'})); }` before finally. Do the same in remove(). In load(), wrap in try/catch/finally and always `setLoading(false)` in finally so a rejected getAll() cannot leave an infinite spinner.

src/screens/admin/AdminSecurityScreen.ts.whatsWrong: In the non-email (phone) branch, `phone.replace('+', '')` and `registerWithPhone({ phone })` dereference `phone`, which comes from `route.params` typed as `any` (line 52 `useRoute<any>()`, line 62 destructure defaulted only to `{}`, never validated). If the email branch is NOT taken and both `whatsapp` and `phone` are undefined, line 118's `phone.replace` throws a TypeError.
src/screens/admin/AdminSecurityScreen.ts.rootCause: Untyped route params + branch logic that assumes `phone` exists whenever the email path isn't taken; no precondition check that a phone number is actually present.
src/screens/admin/AdminSecurityScreen.ts.failureScenario: Screen is reached with params `{ method: 'email', email: '' }` (or any state where `method === 'email' && email` is falsy) and no `phone`/`whatsapp` — e.g. a param renamed upstream, a back-navigation that dropped a field, or a resumed OTP flow. Execution falls into the `else` branch: `whatsapp ? ... : phone.replace('+','')` evaluates `undefined.replace` and throws. It is caught at line 125, so the app doesn't hard-crash, but line 126 surfaces a cryptic `"undefined is not an object (evaluating 'phone.replace')"` to the admin and account creation is permanently blocked with no actionable message.
src/screens/admin/AdminSecurityScreen.ts.fix: Guard before the try and normalize: `const rawPhone = phone ? String(phone) : ''; if (method !== 'email' && !rawPhone) { setErrorMessage(t('auth.adminSetup.fillBothFields', { defaultValue: 'Missing phone number' })); return; }` then use `rawPhone.replace('+','')` and pass `phone: rawPhone` to `registerWithPhone`.

src/screens/admin/AdminSendNotificationS.whatsWrong: The confirm handler awaits `sendNotificationToUsers` with no guard against the screen being popped during the request. Nothing prevents navigating away while `sending` is true — the header back button (192) and hardware back stay live. On slow/no network (realistic in Iraq) the await window is seconds long. When it resolves, `Alert.alert(success, [{ onPress: () => navigation.goBack() }])` (120-122), `setFormData` (124) and `setSending(false)` (136) all run on an unmounted component: a 'Notification sent successfully' Alert pops on top of whatever screen the user is now on, and tapping OK fires `navigation.goBack()` on a stale navigation object (may pop the unrelated screen). Same for the failure Alert (134).
src/screens/admin/AdminSendNotificationS.rootCause: No in-flight lifecycle guard; async closure captures navigation/setState and runs after unmount.
src/screens/admin/AdminSendNotificationS.failureScenario: Admin fills the form, taps Send, confirms. Request is in flight on a slow connection. Admin taps the header back arrow to return to the dashboard. 3s later the request resolves → a 'Success' alert appears over the dashboard, and OK calls goBack() popping the dashboard. Plus a React setState-after-unmount warning.
src/screens/admin/AdminSendNotificationS.fix: Add a mounted ref and gate the post-await work: `const isMountedRef = useRef(true); useEffect(() => () => { isMountedRef.current = false; }, []);` then inside onPress after the await do `if (!isMountedRef.current) return;` before the success Alert/setFormData, and guard `finally { if (isMountedRef.current) setSending(false); }`. Optionally also disable the header back button while `sending` (e.g. `disabled={sending}` on the back TouchableOpacity).

src/screens/admin/AdminSettingsScreen.ts.whatsWrong: The load effect fires two async fetches (storeProfileService.getStoreProfile and the supabase tenants.business_info query) keyed on tenantId with NO cancellation guard. On a rapid tenantId change A→B (owner switching tenants, or re-login without unmount), tenant A's slower response can resolve AFTER tenant B's and call setStoreProfile / setBusinessName, painting tenant A's store name, logo and cover image under tenant B. This directly violates the project golden rule that tenant state must be cleared on tenant change and tenantId must key every fetch/cache.
src/screens/admin/AdminSettingsScreen.ts.rootCause: Async results are committed unconditionally; the effect has no cleanup to ignore stale responses.
src/screens/admin/AdminSettingsScreen.ts.failureScenario: Owner viewing tenant A (slow network) switches active tenant to B. Effect for A and B both run; B resolves first and renders correctly, then A's in-flight getStoreProfile resolves and overwrites the header/logo/cover with tenant A's data while tenantId is B — cross-tenant data leak on screen.
src/screens/admin/AdminSettingsScreen.ts.fix: Add a guard: `useEffect(() => { let cancelled = false; ...reset...; if (tenantId) { storeProfileService.getStoreProfile(tenantId).then(p => { if (!cancelled) setStoreProfile(p); }).catch(...); (async () => { const { data } = await supabase...; if (!cancelled) setBusinessName(info.name || ...); })(); } return () => { cancelled = true; }; }, [tenantId]);`

src/screens/admin/AdminStockReportScreen.whatsWrong: The receivables filter matches status case-sensitively: `o.status === 'delivered'` (124). The revenue calc for the SAME orders matches case-insensitively: `String(order.status || '').toLowerCase() !== 'delivered'` (553). The two disagree on any non-lowercase casing.
src/screens/admin/AdminStockReportScreen.rootCause: Two independently-written status checks in the same file with different normalization.
src/screens/admin/AdminStockReportScreen.failureScenario: An order stored with status 'Delivered' or 'DELIVERED' carrying a $500 unpaid balance is counted in the revenue report but EXCLUDED from receivables — totalUnpaidAmountUSD and the unpaid list understate money owed, so the admin under-collects.
src/screens/admin/AdminStockReportScreen.fix: Normalize the receivables check to match: `return String(o.status || '').toLowerCase() === 'delivered' && remaining > 0.01;`

src/screens/admin/ReportsGenerator.tsx.whatsWrong: Every dynamic string is interpolated raw into the generated PDF HTML with no escaping: customer name/recipient/phone in the unpaid report (L602-604: `${item.name}`, `${item.recipientName}`, `${item.phone}`), product name/part number in the customer invoice (L705: `${name}`, `${it.partNumber}`) and customer name/phone (L778-779), plus company settings and part numbers in the revenue report (L483, L537, L369). shippingAddress.fullName / phone / recipientName are customer-entered at checkout, i.e. attacker-influenced data flowing into an admin document.
src/screens/admin/ReportsGenerator.tsx.rootCause: String-template HTML with no HTML-entity escaping of interpolated values.
src/screens/admin/ReportsGenerator.tsx.failureScenario: A customer checks out with the name `Ali ` or a shop enters a product named `USB 3.0 `. When the owner generates the Unpaid Orders / customer invoice PDF, the browser in expo-print treats `` / `` as an unknown tag: the text after `<` vanishes and, worse, an unclosed tag such as `` or `
src/screens/admin/ReportsGenerator.tsx.fix: Add a helper `const esc = (s:any) => String(s ?? '').replace(/[&<>"']/g, c => ({'&':'&','<':'<','>':'>','"':'"',"'":'''}[c] as string));` and wrap every dynamic interpolation that isn't a number/known-safe: e.g. L602 `${esc(item.name)}`, `${esc(item.recipientName)}`, `${esc(item.phone)}`, L705 `${esc(name)}`/`${esc(it.partNumber)}`, L778-779 `${esc(user?.name || 'N/A')}`/`${esc(user.phone)}`, L477/537 `${esc(L.company)}` and phone/email/address, L369/446 `${esc(r.partNumber || '—')}`.

src/screens/admin/partnerInvoice.ts.whatsWrong: Every dynamic string is interpolated raw into the HTML template with no escaping: productName(p) at line 203, p.partNumber at 204, L.company (admin-entered invoiceSettings.companyName) at 298, the phone/address subtitle at 299, opts.partnerName at 303, and phone/email/website in the footer at 372-374. expo-print renders this HTML in a WebView, so any '<' , '>' or '"' in the data corrupts the surrounding markup.
src/screens/admin/partnerInvoice.ts.rootCause: Template-literal string building interpolates untrusted product/settings text directly into HTML without HTML-entity escaping.
src/screens/admin/partnerInvoice.ts.failureScenario: A product legitimately named '6.5" <OLED> Panel' or a part number like 'MB<123>', or a company/partner name typed by the admin containing '<' or '&' (e.g. 'Ali & <Sons>'), makes the WebView swallow the rest of that table cell (and following tags) as an unclosed tag — the row, or everything after it, renders garbled or blank in the shared PDF. With a '<script>' payload it can even execute in the print WebView.
src/screens/admin/partnerInvoice.ts.fix: Add a helper `const esc = (s: any) => String(s ?? '').replace(/[&<>"']/g, c => ({'&':'&','<':'<','>':'>','"':'"',"'":'''}[c] as string));` and wrap every dynamic value: `${esc(productName(p))}`, `${esc(p.partNumber || 'N/A')}`, `${esc(L.company)}`, `${esc(opts.partnerName)}`, `${esc(L.phone)}`, `${esc(L.email)}`, `${esc(L.website)}`, `${esc(L.address)}` (the base64 image/logo src values are our own and don't need it).
